gloss: Heard with ears and seen with eyes; firsthand experience.
teaser: Ever wondered about the value of firsthand experience? Let's dive in!
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever wondered about the value of firsthand experience? Let's dive in! [break 1s] The phrase is: 耳闻目睹, ěr wén mù dǔ. [break 1s] 耳 (ěr) - ear [break 0.5s] 闻 (wén) - hear [break 0.5s] 目 (mù) - eye [break 0.5s] 睹 (dǔ) - see [break 1s] The full idiom again: 耳闻目睹 means literally 'heard with ears and seen with eyes' and figuratively refers to having firsthand experience. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom comes from ancient times when people relied heavily on direct observation and auditory information. It emphasizes the importance of experiencing events personally rather than relying on hearsay. Many historical texts highlight the value of being an eyewitness to events, as it often leads to more credible accounts. Over time, this idiom became a staple in conversations about truth and reliability. [break 1.5s] Here are three examples: 你可以相信她的故事，因为她是耳闻目睹的。 [break 1s] You can trust her story because she witnessed it firsthand. [break 1s] 我耳闻目睹了整个事件，所以我能告诉你真相。 [break 1s] I saw the whole incident firsthand, so I can tell you the truth. [break 1s] 有些事情只有耳闻目睹才能理解。 [break 1s] Some things can only be understood through firsthand experience. [break 1s] So remember, 耳闻目睹 means firsthand experience. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
